claim: Bonelli-Landier's three decay determinants (liquidity, slow signal-decay, frictionless Sharpe) are exactly the axes of our OBSERVABLE free-data friction index, and predict cross-asset survival.
title: The Capacity of Trading Strategies — battery test
predicts: An observable-friction index built from their determinants (spread/ADV liquidity x signal-decay x turnover x breadth) is monotonically related to net survival across the battery, AND — the make-or-break test — adds explanatory power BEYOND turnover alone (partial-R^2 > 0). If friction collapses to turnover, the frontier degrades to NMV's known turnover sort.
rationale: Supplies the theoretical performance-to-scale object with the exact liquidity/decay/frictionless-Sharpe axes; our contribution renders it as a measured cross-asset cross-sectional survival boundary on free data and tests friction != turnover.

claim: The zeroing-in collapse generalizes cross-asset on FREE data via the ordered rigor waterfall (OOS -> cost -> multiplicity -> capacity).
title: Zeroing In on the Expected Returns of Anomalies — battery test

evidence.measured: DIRECTIONALLY CONFIRMED: net survival ~0 across the free-data cross-asset battery (zero survivors), generalizing the zeroing-in collapse beyond US equities. CAVEAT: our headline is already OOS-honest (~0), so the collapse is shallow vs their 68->4 bps in-sample cascade; the destroyer here is low starting alpha + capacity, not (as CV) spreads.

predicts: Pooled net Deflated Sharpe across the free-data cross-asset battery is indistinguishable from zero after the four rungs — mirroring the ~4 bps terminal cascade rung — across equities/bonds/FX/commodities/crypto, not just US equities.
rationale: The waterfall reproduces their cascade but (a) cross-asset, (b) single-engine, (c) with the four ordered rungs and a capacity rung they omit. This is the closest prior art; our differentiator is scope + the ordered decomposition.

claim: Chen-Zimmermann's optimistic "98% reproduce" is a GROSS in-sample statement that the waterfall guts.
title: chen-zimmermann-open-source-2022 — battery test
predicts: Signals that reproduce gross in-sample on free data (their pole) lose ~all significance at the net + multiplicity + capacity rungs — reproduction fidelity and net survival are different questions, and our oracle is the latter.
rationale: Distinguishes reproduction (their contribution) from survival (ours); the prediction is the gap between the two is nearly the whole gross alpha.

claim: The multiple-testing collapse reproduces cross-asset under our best-of-N / Deflated-Sharpe gate.
title: p-Hacking: Evidence from Two Million Trading Strategies — battery test
predicts: The count of battery families passing the multiplicity-corrected gate is <= what the false-discovery rate predicts under the global null given the total number of specifications tested across the battery.
rationale: Frames our DSR/best-of-N as the cross-asset analogue of their MHT collapse; the survivor count is bounded by chance.

claim: The netting rescue is the strongest counter to our null: a cost-aware COMBINATION of battery anomalies may survive even when every standalone anomaly dies.
title: A Transaction-Cost Perspective on the Multitude of Firm Characteristics — battery test
predicts: A net-of-cost combined book across the battery (trades netted across families) has materially better net Deflated Sharpe than the average standalone family — but STILL fails the multiplicity-corrected survival gate on free data. If it survives, our headline null is falsified and this becomes the finding.
rationale: We must run the netted-combination test explicitly; it is the adversarial best case for anomaly survival and the referee's first objection.

claim: Costs RE-ORDER conclusions cross-asset — the positive structural "failure-fingerprint" result.
title: Model Comparison with Transaction Costs — battery test

evidence.measured: FINGERPRINT present but MODEST + constant-sensitive: commodity families are selection/multiplicity-dominated (d_sel~0.13, d_mult~0.15) while crypto/equity are capacity-dominated (d_cap~0.36/1.16). Directionally supports "the failure mechanism differs by asset class" but depends on the impact constant and is underpowered at ~4 asset classes.

predicts: The RANK of which rigor rung destroys the most alpha differs systematically by asset class: cost/friction-dominated in high-friction commodities and crypto; multiplicity/decay-dominated in mature, heavily-arbitraged equities. The failure MECHANISM fingerprints the market's arbitrage maturity.
rationale: Detzel-NMV establish "costs re-order" for models; we extend "the ordering of destruction is itself informative" across asset classes. Descriptive at ~5 asset classes (not a powered test).

claim: The free-data observable-friction index is a usable proxy for the FIM impact function's cross-sectional ORDERING (not its levels).
title: Trading Costs — battery test
predicts: The friction index rank-correlates positively with the FIM square-root-impact ordering on overlapping liquid equity/futures names; where they diverge we down-weight. This validation defuses the "you cannot measure impact on free data" objection.
rationale: Directly answers the single most attackable element of the frontier (agent-3 caveat #2): we measure OBSERVABLE friction and validate its ordering against the proprietary impact benchmark.

claim: FIM's "survives at scale" verdict is scope-limited to proprietary-execution, deep-liquidity equity implementations.
title: Trading Costs of Asset Pricing Anomalies — battery test

evidence.measured: CONFIRMED on free data: the high-capacity / low-friction multi-asset factor families (riskparity, tsmom, globalfactors, lowvol) fail t>3 despite sitting at the low-friction corner — high capacity does NOT rescue survival on retail-accessible data. FIM "survives at scale" is scope-limited to proprietary-execution equity.

predicts: The free-data, retail-accessible analogues of size/value/momentum land at the HIGH-capacity / low-friction corner of our frontier yet STILL fail net survival — because the surviving alpha lives in the low-capacity names the free-data universe structurally excludes. High capacity does not rescue survival on retail data.
rationale: Places FIM as the optimistic pole our friction frontier arbitrates: the frontier predicts survival only in the LOW-capacity corner, the opposite of where FIM says the big factors live.

claim: The Harvey-Liu haircut is the multiplicity rung of the waterfall and agrees with the Deflated Sharpe on the survivor set.
title: Backtesting — battery test

evidence.measured: The multiplicity gate leaves zero survivors, BUT with the honest trial count (distinct configs) the DSR/haircut rung is MINOR — the zoo dies from low free-data gross alpha + capacity, not primarily from multiplicity. Multiplicity confirms, but is not the mechanism here.

predicts: Families passing nominal t>2 FAIL the haircut threshold once the true trial count (all specs across the battery) is used; haircut and Deflated Sharpe select the same (near-empty) survivor set.
rationale: Operationalizes the multiplicity rung; cross-checks the DSR gate.

claim: HXZ's "most anomalies fail with proper method" holds cross-asset and tightens under costs.
title: hou-xue-zhang-replicating-anomalies-2020 — battery test
predicts: On the free-data cross-asset battery the failure rate meets or exceeds HXZ's 65% (t>1.96) / 82% (t>2.78) once the cost + capacity rungs are added — the equity-only pessimistic pole generalizes.
rationale: HXZ is the "most false" pole; our waterfall shows their conclusion is if anything conservative once costs/capacity/cross-asset enter.

claim: Their cost-bent portfolio frontier and our cross-sectional friction-survival boundary are complementary renderings of the same limit — but ours is a distinct object.
title: Machine Learning and the Implementable Efficient Frontier — battery test
predicts: Plotting each battery anomaly at (observable friction / implied capacity, net Deflated Sharpe) yields a monotone survival BOUNDARY (a fitted quantile envelope, not an eyeballed scatter); unlike their portfolio frontier it is per-anomaly, cross-sectional, and cross-asset.
rationale: The nearest geometric prior art; we must state precisely why the object differs (cross-sectional survival boundary vs MV frontier) to claim the frontier as novel.

claim: JKP's "no replication crisis" is an artifact of cost-free, index-level, pre-capacity construction.
title: jensen-kelly-pedersen-replication-crisis-2023 — battery test
predicts: JKP's ~82% replication rate collapses toward the HXZ pole once the fixed cost + multiplicity + capacity rungs are imposed on the same signals cross-asset — the optimism does not survive the waterfall.
rationale: Our design arbitrates the HXZ-vs-JKP standoff; the prediction is that "no crisis" is a discipline artifact, not a market fact.

claim: McLean-Pontiff post-publication decay is the DECAY rung and generalizes cross-asset.
title: mclean-pontiff-decay-2016 — battery test
predicts: Battery families show OOS/post-publication shrinkage on the order of MP's 26% (OOS) / 58% (post-pub) as a distinct rung of the waterfall, cross-asset — decay is a first-class destroyer alongside cost, not a substitute.
rationale: MP owns decay; we place it as one ordered rung and confirm it is separable from the cost rung in the attribution.

claim: Our single-engine, single-cost-model design is the controlled INVERSE of Non-Standard Errors: hold the evidence-generating process to ~zero so surviving dispersion is attributable to the anomaly and asset, not the analyst.
title: Nonstandard Errors — battery test
predicts: Within a single anomaly, the specification-curve spread across defensible analyst choices is LARGE (confirming Menkveld) BUT its center is statistically indistinguishable from zero net alpha — dispersion is analyst noise around a null, not disagreement about a real effect.
rationale: The spec-grid measures per-anomaly dispersion; the harness reports median (honest) vs max (cherry-picked) net DSR and the two-sided distance of the spec-curve center from zero.

claim: NMV's inverse turnover-survival relation is the seed of the friction frontier — but friction adds signal beyond turnover.
title: novy-marx-velikov-taxonomy-costs-2016 — battery test

evidence.measured: PARTIAL: a weak turnover-survival relation is present (turnover alone R2~0.29 on net Sharpe) but the observable friction index does NOT significantly reorder survival beyond turnover (partial-R2 5.6%, F=0.61, p~0.56). At N=18 families the frontier is underpowered to distinguish from NMV's turnover sort — the make-or-break objection is NOT overcome on current evidence.

predicts: Net survival is monotone in the observable-friction index cross-asset (extending NMV's turnover buckets to a continuous boundary), AND the friction index reorders survival relative to a pure turnover sort (partial-R^2 of spread/ADV/breadth beyond turnover > 0).
rationale: NMV supplies the mechanism and the make-or-break objection (frontier != turnover repackaged); our contribution is the continuous cross-asset boundary that beats the turnover sort.

claim: Specification-curve joint inference applied to each anomaly rejects the naive single-spec point estimate in favor of the honest curve median.
title: Specification Curve Analysis — battery test
predicts: The whole-curve permutation test FAILS to reject the global null of no net effect for all but the lowest-capacity corner; the spec-curve MEDIAN net DSR (not the cherry-picked max) is ~0 for ~all families.
rationale: The imported method IS leg-1 of the harness (the fragility surface). The prediction is that honest joint inference nulls the zoo.

claim: A secular-trend confound inflates apparent anomaly alpha cross-asset, and the true survivor is trend-orthogonal (market-neutral).
title: The Factor Multiverse: The Role of Interest Rates in Factor Return Measurement — battery test
predicts: Benchmarking the battery's directional books against the dominant secular trend in each asset class (the multi-decade rate move for rate-sensitive books; the equity/crypto bull drift) shrinks residual alpha toward zero; the survivor is the market-neutral commodity value residual, consistent with our characterization.
rationale: Their duration-matched adjustment motivates a per-asset-class secular-trend control in the waterfall; the residual must be trend-orthogonal to count.
